images.title: Switch one sign, the value moves by 2 × 4
images.purpose: Shows that switching one sign changes the value by twice the switched number, so the parity stays the same.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Two expressions stacked one above the other, before on top and after below, with one bracket showing the change.
images.exact_structure: Top line, large dark text: 3 + 4 − 5 − 6 = −4, with the +4 drawn in green (#009E73). Bottom line, directly below and aligned term by term: 3 − 4 − 5 − 6 = −12, with the −4 drawn in vermilion (#D55E00). A thin reddish purple (#CC79A7) ring circles the sign in front of 4 on each line, and a short reddish purple (#CC79A7) arrow points down from the top ring to the bottom ring. To the right of both lines, a reddish purple (#CC79A7) bracket joins the two results −4 and −12 and carries the label change 8 = 2 × 4. Under the bottom line, centred, the label both even. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Switching +4 to −4 moves the value by 8, an even number, so the parity does not change.
images.description: Shows that switching one sign changes the value by twice the switched number, so the parity stays the same.

image_decisions.why: A before and after pair with the change bracketed makes the 2b argument visible with the concept's own numbers.
